runbooks.diagnosis: Camunda cannot reach PostgreSQL. The JDBC datasource is configured via DB_URL/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD and the container starts before postgres is ready, or the credentials are wrong.
remediation: Verify postgres is healthy: docker inspect opensme-postgres-1
Verify DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD match the postgres-init users
Restart camunda after postgres is healthy

runbooks.diagnosis: Camunda JVM heap exhausted. Default JVM heap is too small for large process definitions or high-throughput deployments, or the container memory limit is too low.
remediation: Increase the container memory limit in services/camunda.yml
Set JAVA_OPTS to increase -Xmx (e.g. -Xmx768m) if the default is too low
Check for runaway process instances or infinite loops in BPMN

runbooks.diagnosis: Camunda/Tomcat failed during startup — usually a missing database table (first-run schema setup), a port conflict on 8080, or a corrupt deployment.
remediation: Check logs for the exact startup phase that failed
If first run, ensure the database schema was created (Camunda auto-creates on first boot)
Verify port 8080 is not already in use by another container
Clear the camunda-data volume only if you accept data loss

runbooks.diagnosis: The REST API is not deployed or the context path is wrong. Camunda 7 serves REST at /engine-rest/engine by default.
remediation: Verify the REST API war is deployed (check /camunda/lib or the webapps directory)
Check if the Tomcat connector is on 8080 and the Traefik rule routes bpm.* correctly
